subtopic: Handling a legal or tax notice
subtype: Approach: verifying authenticity through official channels [Action]
passage:
The email said a notice was waiting and gave a big blue button. Gopika read it twice in the living room of her flat in Bengaluru, and something felt off.
"Don't click, Tejas," she said as her flatmate leaned over. "There's a lot of fake notices going round."
She opened a fresh browser tab and typed the official portal address herself. She logged in with her own details and looked in the section for notices. Nothing there.
Then she went back to the email and found the sender's address was slightly wrong. She used the email's report option, deleted it, and told Tejas, "If it's real, it'll be in the portal too."
Tejas nodded and moved his laptop away from the email.

qa.q: Where did Gopika read the email?
qa.a: Gopika read it in the living room of her flat in Bengaluru.

qa.q: What was Gopika feeling as she read the email a second time?
qa.a: Gopika felt uneasy and suspicious, sensing that something was off before knowing why.

qa.q: What could Gopika do if the notice does appear on the portal?
qa.a: Gopika could read it there, note the date it asks for a reply, and talk to a qualified tax practitioner if it is unclear.

qa.q: How might Tejas have felt seeing Gopika check the portal?
qa.a: Tejas was probably curious and somewhat relieved, since he was about to lean in to the email and later moved his laptop away.

grounding: The passage shows a person who, aware of fake notices, opens the official portal directly and checks for the notice instead of clicking email links.

'Anand bhaiya, look! Tax department. They say there's a refund adjustment, click here to update bank details in 24 hours!' Madhav pushed the phone across the table.
Anand didn't touch the link. 'Who sent it?'
'Income tax something dot in.'
'Something. Read it slowly.'
Madhav squinted. 'Income-tax-refund-help. Oh.'
'Open the real portal. Type the address yourself.'
'Why can't I just click?'
'Because if it's fake, clicking is the problem.' Anand watched Madhav log in with his own password. 'Now go to pending actions. Anything there?'
Madhav scrolled. 'Nothing. No notice, no demand.'
'Then it's not real. Report it, delete it, and tell Ma not to click anything like this either.'
Madhav let out a long breath and laughed a little. 'Twenty-four hours. It really got me.'

qa.q: What did Madhav find under pending actions?
How was Madhav feeling when he pushed the phone across the table?
qa.a: Madhav was alarmed and rushed by the 24-hour deadline, which is exactly the pressure a fake notice relies on.

qa.q: What else could Anand and Madhav do after deleting the email?
qa.a: They could report it through the official channel and set up alerts on the real portal, so any genuine notice is seen there first.

qa.q: How might Ma be affected by Anand's last instruction?
qa.a: Ma gets a simple warning that may protect her from a similar fake link that uses fear and a deadline.

grounding: It shows someone who knows fake notices exist checking the official portal directly instead of clicking an email link.

passage:
I'm Jyoti, and last month an email nearly got me. It had the tax department's logo, my full name and the last four digits of my PAN, and it said a demand of 18,400 rupees was pending, with a payment link 'to avoid penalty'. My hand was on the trackpad when I remembered Mridul at work, who had paid a fake 'notice' last year and never got the money back.
So I closed the email. I opened a new tab and typed the tax portal's address myself, letter by letter. I logged in and checked the notices section. There was nothing. No demand, no pending anything. I called the helpline number printed on the portal, not the one in the email, and they confirmed it. I forwarded the email to the reporting address and deleted it. Then I messaged Mridul: 'You saved me eighteen thousand today.'

qa.q: What demand did the email say was pending?
qa.a: A demand of 18,400 rupees, with a payment link to avoid penalty.

qa.q: What made Jyoti stop with a hand on the trackpad, and how did Jyoti feel then?
qa.a: Remembering Mridul's loss made Jyoti suspicious and uneasy, enough to pause instead of paying.

qa.q: Which step in Jyoti's approach mattered most, and why?
qa.a: Typing the portal's address directly and checking the notices section, because a fake email cannot fake what is on the real portal.

qa.q: How might Mridul feel on getting Jyoti's message?
qa.a: Mridul may feel a mix of old regret and warmth 🙂 glad that a painful loss helped a colleague avoid the same trap.

grounding: It shows someone aware of fake notices logging in to the official portal directly to check a demand rather than clicking an email link.
